issue: Does the word "and" in the First Step Act's safety-valve provision, 18 U.S.C. § 3553(f)(1), mean that a defendant must satisfy all listed criteria (conjunctive), or may it be read as "or" (disjunctive), so that a defendant who satisfies only one criterion is eligible for the safety valve?

sides.position: "And" is unambiguously conjunctive: a defendant must satisfy all of the § 3553(f)(1) criteria to qualify for relief from the statutory minimum.
cases: United States v. Palomares, 52 F.4th 640 (5th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Haynes, 2022 WL 17750939 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Pulsifer, 39 F.4th 1018 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Lopez, 58 F.4th 1108 (9th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: "And" means "or" (disjunctive) in § 3553(f)(1), so a defendant need not satisfy every criterion to qualify for the safety valve.
cases: United States v. Pace, 48 F.4th 741 (7th Cir. 2022)

this_court: The panel holds that "and" in § 3553(f)(1) is unambiguously conjunctive, so the conjunctive side.
quote: Courts and judges around the country have split on this issue. Given the deep split, this issue warrants Supreme Court review.
cite: United States v. Eric Lopez, 58 F.4th 1108 (9th Cir. 2023)
